subject: Performance commitments – latency SLO exceptions & order form language
messages:
From: Rachel Stein <rachel.stein@carebridge.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@carebridge.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Performance commitments -- request for latency SLO exceptions & order form language

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's routing and cache features. Procurement has one remaining ask before we can approve the order form: CareBridge needs a narrow latency SLO exception for a single high-throughput route that powers our triage UI. Specifically: we want a 95th/99th percentile latency target for the /v1/triage/generate endpoint, and an explicit burst/overload tolerance clause (how many concurrent requests before degraded behavior triggers).

We can accept a limited availability exception for that route if you can:
- Add an order-form exhibit enumerating the /v1/triage/generate SLOs (p95=200ms, p99=450ms) and a defined burst window (30s, with graceful degradation to p99<900ms).
- Provide an evidence package (sample tail-latency report and a short runbook for incidents).
- Limit the exception to a single quoted environment (prod-us-east-1) and have automatic failover to a compatible model with clear rollback criteria.

Attached is a redline of the order form and MSA exhibit — we'd like to close this week. Can you confirm whether Redwood can make the exhibit change and what evidence you can provide?

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Stein
VP Product, CareBridge Health
Procurement: procurement@carebridge.com

Attachments: CareBridge_SLA_Redlines.docx

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. We can work with a constrained exception but need to line up a few internal checks first. Quick answers up front:

- Order-form exhibit: yes, we can add a route-specific exhibit that calls out p95/p99 & burst window language — prefer to phrase as target ranges with an operational tolerance to avoid hard legal guarantees on tail percentiles.
- Evidence: we can attach a sample tail-latency report (aditya will provide) and a short incident runbook.
- Scope: we can limit to prod-us-east-1 and add automatic routing to a lower-throughput model variant as fallback.

Next steps: can we set a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk procurement through the proposed exhibit language? Ben will coordinate procurement/legal flow. I'll loop in Markus from Legal once we have the exact phrasing so he can assess risk and any required offsets in the order form (credits, scope limits).

Thanks — Naomi

Naomi / Ben — looping in some technical constraints and a proposed draft for the exhibit.

Key technical notes:
- Tail latency percentiles are sensitive to sequence length and model variant. For the /v1/triage/generate route we need to pin the model family and max tokens to make a meaningful p95/p99 commitment.
- For burst tolerance, we can define a configurable burst window (30s) and a concurrency cap per-customer. During burst saturation we offer two behaviors: degrade to a smaller model variant (faster but lower throughput quality) OR queue requests (adds latency). We recommend degrade+fallback rather than queuing for triage UI to keep UI responsiveness.

Proposed exhibit language (high level, for legal to format):
- "Route-specific Performance Exhibit: Redwood will target median/p95/p99 latency targets for the named API route when used with the specified model family and request shape. These targets are operational goals and subject to documented tolerances for burst windows and model fallbacks. Where an exception is granted, the exception will be scoped to the named environment and traffic profile. Redwood will provide monthly sample tail-latency reports and a runbook for incident response."

I've attached a sample tail-latency report from a prior customer (anonymized) and a redlined order form mock-up that shows how we usually present the exhibit. If Procurement wants hard numbers in the order form (p95=200ms, p99=450ms), Legal should include a fallback paragraph that specifies when the target is no longer guaranteed (sustained load over rolling 5 minute window or failed GPU availability).

Attachments: sample-tail-latency-report.pdf, redlined-order-form.pdf

Happy to join the procurement sync.
- Aditya

Team / Rachel — thanks for drafting. From Legal's perspective we can accept a route-level exhibit but recommend the following concrete controls to limit risk: 

1) Make all p95/p99 values "target" language with explicit operational tolerances and an exclusion for sustained incidents caused by third-party cloud outages.
2) Cap scope: exception limited to prod-us-east-1, single order form / single associated environment; add a clause that new routes or additional environments require separate negotiation.
3) Include an automatic fallback & rollback clause: if fallback is triggered more than X times in a rolling 30-day window (we recommend X=5), Redwood will trigger a remediation plan and the parties will re-evaluate the exhibit (option to revert to standard SLOs or change credits).
4) Limit financial exposure: make credits capped (not unlimited) and proportionate to the affected route's allocated quota.

I'll draft redline language for sections 4 and 7 of the order form and attach to the follow-up. If procurement wants hard numbers baked in, we should attach a short definition appendix that ties the metric to request shape (max tokens, model family) to avoid later disputes.

Markus Klein
